newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares add on but gains seen capped.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares add on but gains seen capped.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose for the fifth day in a row, closing 0.38 percent higher on Tuesday, but traders said gains were likely to be short-lived.
"Prices fell too much over a short period so today's rise can still be seen as a technical rebound, but I can't see any reason for a further rise," one broker said.
The SBI index rose 0.38 percent or 4.65 points to 1,228.3, taking its gains to 3.19 percent over the last five sessions.
"I don't think the market will react immediately to the ratification of the EU accord on July 15. It may only have an impact longer term," said Davor Dubokovic, a trader at Eastbrokers.
Parliament is expected to change the constitution by July 15 which would open the way for speedy ratification of the EU association treaty, signed last year.
Overall seven shares rose, 13 fell and one was flat, while eight were untraded. Turnover rose to 58.8 million tolars from 41.3 million.
Drug maker Lek was the most active, easing 0.43 percent to 22,900 tolars on volume of 775 shares for total turnover of 17.9 million tolars.
"Lek is for sure one of Slovenia's best companies and also among the most interesting for foreign investors, and at current prices is very low," Dubokovic said.
Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, jumping 8.30 percent to 7,700 tolars on volume of only 21 shares.
Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska Banka led the day's decliners, tumbling 9.35 percent to 12,500 tolars on volume of 80 shares.
"I do not see any particular reason for the bank's fall, except for low liquidity, a problem common to many Slovenian banks," one trader said.
